messages.subject: Standardized latent variable
parts:
Hello,
I have a question about the standardization of latent variable when i use the cfa fonction.,
When we make the summary, the estimate of the first manifest variable of every latent variable is always = 1.000. 
I want to know if it's possible to change this and to put the higest estimate = 1,000  and not the first.
Thank you for your answer

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: Standardized latent variable
parts:
Hi
I am not sure what is your mean by 'to put the highest estimate=1,000 and not the firs'. but i assume your mean is setting latent variable variance and mean to 1 and 0 prospectively for identification, instead of fixing the first indicator loading and intercept to 1 and 0. if so, for doing it simply use std.lv=TRUE in your cfa or sem function. for example:
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, std.lv = TRUE)   

if you want to put the loading of other indicator to 1 instead of the first one simply insert 1 before it in your model and insert NA* before the first one. for example:
model <- ’ ind60 =~ NA*x1 + x2 + 1*x3 
                dem60 =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3 + 1*y4
'   
HTH
